study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals were estimated for each functional connection in healthy controls. A 90% tolerance proportion with a 10% confidence level was set.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we used the 'tolerance' package in R... to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs. Following prior studies, we set a 90% tolerance proportion with a 10% confidence level
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Fang2025.pdf.md: Identifying extreme functional connections in MDD

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Pairwise Pearson's correlation coefficients between regional signals (200 regions, Craddock atlas), transformed to Fisher's Z scores.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Functional networks were estimated by calculating pairwise Pearson's correlation coefficients between regional signals, with the resulting values transformed to Fisher' Z scores. This procedure produced a 200 × 200 functional connectivity matrix for each participant.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Fang2025.pdf.md: Functional connectivity features and harmonization

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The study utilized nonparametric tolerance intervals on harmonized data (using ComBat for site effects) without explicitly modeling explanatory variables like age or sex in the normative model itself.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we used the 'tolerance' package in R... to estimate nonparametric two-sided tolerance intervals for each functional connection in HCs.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Fang2025.pdf.md: Identifying extreme functional connections in MDD
